svg.aria-label: The three commands of the five minute try: the install, the companion demonstration in two processes, and the dissociation protocol on the organ alone
svg.title: Try it in five minutes: what each command plays
svg.text: Try it in five minutes: what each command plays
quantum-cortex, original figure. No checkpoint is needed: the organ and the protocols run on a CPU, in seconds.
pip install quantum-cortex
the first command
Installs the organ and the protocols
the journal, the write gate, the cue index, the lifecycle, the dissociation protocol, the provenance benchmark; no weights are downloaded
python -m cortex_c2b.companion_demo
the second command: the organ as a component
Session one writes
a project's decisions, line by line,
into a sealed journal on disk
The process ends
only the disk remains
Session two, a new process, reads the disk
it answers what it was told by citing the stored line with its pointer,
and says "no record" for what it was never told
python -m cortex_c2b.hm_protocol --persistent
the third command: the protocol the record is built on
The dissociation protocol runs against the organ alone, in four arms
journal on: planted facts must come back · journal off: they must vanish ·
never planted names: claims must stay rare · the skill arm: the rest must not move
It prints its verdict
PASS or FAIL; a failure is a result
thresholds frozen before any run
What the five minutes show, and what they do not
They show the organ's own code path: a fact written in one process is found by another, by its address, and cited by its pointer; what was never written gets "no record".

They do not run the language model (the checkpoints are not part of the package) and they are not a benchmark score: the record's numbers are in its rows, each with the file that produced it and the test that recomputes it.
The twenty minute way to attack the published numbers, with the command that recomputes each of them, is docs/FALSIFY.md.
